cues.en: Space travel is the most exciting and challenging adventure humanity has ever undertaken.
cues.zh: 太空旅行是人类进行过最激动人心、最具挑战性的冒险。

cues.en: But in an irony of history, we may stop ourselves from going into space the more we do it.
cues.zh: 但具有历史讽刺意味的是，我们越是进行太空探索，可能越会阻碍自己走向太空。

cues.en: With every rocket launched and with every satellite deployed,
cues.zh: 随着每一枚火箭的发射和每一颗卫星的部署，

cues.en: we're creating a trap for ourselves that gets deadlier and more dangerous every year.
cues.zh: 我们正在为自己设下一个陷阱，它一年比一年更致命、更危险。

cues.en: If it's ever activated,
cues.zh: 如果这个陷阱一旦被触发，

cues.en: it could end the space age and trap us on our planet for decades or even centuries.
cues.zh: 它可能会终结太空时代，把我们困在地球上数十年甚至数个世纪。

cues.en: Getting something into space is incredibly hard. To do so, you need to move very, very fast. At first, straight up to leave the atmosphere, then sideways to begin a sort of circling around the Earth, still very, very fast.
cues.zh: 把东西送入太空极其困难。为此，你需要以极快、极快的速度运动。起初是垂直向上冲出大气层，接着是横向飞行，开始绕地球某种形式的盘旋，速度依然非常非常快。

cues.en: If you do that successfully, you can enter a low Earth orbit.
cues.zh: 如果你成功做到这一点，就能进入近地轨道。

cues.en: And once in orbit, it's very hard to get out of orbit.
cues.zh: 而一旦进入轨道，想要脱离轨道就非常困难。

cues.en: Unless you have energy to spare, you're sort of locked in here, falling around the Earth forever.
cues.zh: 除非你有富余的能量，否则你基本上就被锁在这里，永远在地球周围下坠。

cues.en: That's great for things we want to stay up, like space stations and satellites.
cues.zh: 这对我们希望留在空中的东西来说是件好事，比如空间站和卫星。

cues.en: And so we moved the majority of humanity's space infrastructure to this place, just a few 100 kilometers above the surface.
cues.zh: 因此，我们将人类绝大部分的太空基础设施都转移到了这个地方——距离地表仅几百公里的高空。

cues.en: Just high enough so that the atmosphere is so thin that orbiting things can stay up for centuries before air resistance can slow them enough to bring them back to Earth.
cues.zh: 这里的高度刚刚好，大气稀薄到让轨道运行物能够停留数个世纪，然后空气阻力才会将其减速并带回地球。

cues.en: But this is also the source of our deadly trap.
cues.zh: 但这同时也是我们致命陷阱的根源。

cues.en: Rockets are really metal cylinders that keep big piles of fuel in place. When ever a portion of the fuel has been spent, the empty tanks are dropped to make the rocket lighter.
cues.zh: 火箭实际上就是把大量燃料固定在位的金属圆筒。每当一部分燃料用完，空燃料箱就会被抛弃，以减轻火箭的重量。

cues.en: Some parts crash down to earth or burn up in the atmosphere.
cues.zh: 有些部分坠回地面或在大气层中烧毁。

cues.en: But most of the useless rocket parts stay up and begin to orbit the planet.
cues.zh: 但大多数无用的火箭残件留在空中，开始环绕地球运行。

cues.en: After decades of space travel, low Earth orbit is a junkyard of spent boosters,
cues.zh: 经过几十年的太空探索，近地轨道已经成了废弃助推器的垃圾场，

cues.en: broken satellites, and millions of pieces of shrapnel from missile tests and explosions.
cues.zh: 这里有损坏的卫星，以及来自导弹试验和爆炸的数百万片弹片。

cues.en: Right now, we know of around 2,600
cues.zh: 目前，我们已知大约有 2,600 个

cues.en: defunct satellites, 10,000 objects bigger than a monitor, 20,000 as large as an apple, 500,000
cues.zh: 失效卫星、10,000 个比显示器大的物体、20,000 个和苹果一样大的物体、500,000 个

cues.en: pieces the size of a marble, and at least 100,000,000
cues.zh: 弹珠大小的碎片，以及至少 1 亿个

cues.en: parts so small they can't be tracked.
cues.zh: 小到无法追踪的零件。

cues.en: This debris is moving at speeds of up to 30,000
cues.zh: 这些碎片以高达每小时 30,000

cues.en: kilometers per hour, circling Earth on crisscrossing orbits multiple times a day.
cues.zh: 公里的速度移动，在交错的轨道上每天绕地球数圈。

cues.en: Orbital speeds are so fast that being hit by debris the size of a pea is like being shot by a plasma gun. On impact, the debris vaporizes,
cues.zh: 轨道速度极快，被豌豆大小的碎片击中就像被等离子枪射击一样。撞击时，碎片会瞬间气化，

cues.en: releasing enough energy to punch holes straight through solid metal.
cues.zh: 释放出足以直接击穿实心金属的能量。

cues.en: So we've covered the space around our planet with millions of pieces of destruction.
cues.zh: 所以，我们在地球周围布满了数百万个破坏性碎片。

cues.en: And we also put a trillion dollar global infrastructure network right in the danger zone.
cues.zh: 而且我们还将价值万亿美元的全球基础设施网络直接置于危险区域。

cues.en: It performs critical duties essential to the modern world. Global communication,
cues.zh: 它执行着现代世界不可或缺的关键任务。全球通信、

cues.en: GPS and navigation,
cues.zh: GPS 与导航、

cues.en: collecting weather data,
cues.zh: 收集气象数据、

cues.en: looking out for asteroids,
cues.zh: 监视小行星，

cues.en: and all manner of scientific discoveries.
cues.zh: 以及各种科学发现。

cues.en: Things we would miss very much if they suddenly went away.
cues.zh: 如果它们突然消失，我们会非常怀念。

cues.en: If just one piece sized bullet hits one of our 1,100
cues.zh: 只要有一颗子弹大小的碎片击中我们 1,100 个

cues.en: working satellites, it will be destroyed instantly.
cues.zh: 工作卫星中的一个，它就会瞬间被毁。

cues.en: Three or four satellites are already being destroyed this way every year.
cues.zh: 每年已经有三到四颗卫星以这种方式被摧毁。

cues.en: As the number of satellites and the amount of junk in orbit is expected to grow tenfold in the next decade, we're approaching a tipping point.
cues.zh: 随着未来十年轨道上的卫星数量和太空垃圾数量预计将增长十倍，我们正在接近一个临界点。

cues.en: But the worst thing in space is not tiny pieces of junk. The worst thing would be an unstoppable chain reaction that turns turns a lot of non junk things into junk.
cues.zh: 但太空中最可怕的不是微小的太空垃圾。最糟糕的是无法阻挡的链式反应，它会把大量非垃圾的东西变成垃圾。

cues.en: For example, if two satellites hit each other in just the right way.
cues.zh: 例如，如果两颗卫星以恰到好处的方式相撞。

cues.en: If satellites collide,
cues.zh: 如果卫星相撞，

cues.en: they don't stop and fall out of the sky. It's more of a splash than a crash.
cues.zh: 它们不会停下来并从天空中坠落。这与其说是碰撞，不如说是四溅。

cues.en: Orbital speeds are so fast, solid pieces spray right through each other, transforming the two satellites into clouds of thousands of little things still fast enough to destroy more satellites.
cues.zh: 轨道速度极快，固体碎片会直接穿透彼此，将这两颗卫星变成数千个小物体组成的云团，它们的速度仍然足以摧毁更多卫星。

cues.en: This could trigger the slowest and most destructive sort of domino effect, a collision cascade.
cues.zh: 这可能会引发最缓慢、最具破坏性的多米诺骨牌效应——碰撞级联。

cues.en: Like a shotgun spray, each collision creates more bullets. What was once a single tiny target, very unlikely to hit anything, becomes a wall of destruction, hungry to make more.
cues.zh: 就像散弹枪喷射一样，每一次碰撞都会产生更多的子弹。曾经那个极难击中任何东西的单一微小目标，变成了一堵毁灭之墙，渴望制造更多破坏。

cues.en: As more and more satellites are destroyed, the destruction accelerates exponentially,
cues.zh: 随着越来越多的卫星被摧毁，毁灭的速度呈指数级加快，

cues.en: eventually destroying everything parked in orbit.
cues.zh: 最终摧毁停留在轨道上的所有东西。

cues.en: But space is very empty, so the first few collisions may take a long time.
cues.zh: 但太空非常空旷，所以前几次碰撞可能需要很长时间。

cues.en: By the time we realize what's happening, it's too late.
cues.zh: 等我们意识到发生了什么时，已经太晚了。

cues.en: One year, one satellite is destroyed, and that's no big deal. The next year, five.
cues.zh: 第一年，有一颗卫星被摧毁，这没什么大不了的。第二年，五颗。

cues.en: The year after, fifty, until there's nothing left.
cues.zh: 再过一年，五十，直到什么都不剩。

cues.en: The situation in orbit is rapidly worsening, and we may already be past the point of no return.
cues.zh: 轨道上的情况正在迅速恶化，我们可能已经越过了不可逆转的临界点。

cues.en: Within ten years, space around Earth may no longer be viable for long term satellites or rockets.
cues.zh: 十年之内，地球周围的太空可能不再适合长期卫星或火箭运行。

cues.en: The worst case scenario is horrifying.
cues.zh: 最坏的情况令人恐惧。

cues.en: A debris field made of hundreds of millions of pieces, many too small to track, moving at 30,000
cues.zh: 一个由数亿碎片组成的碎片场，其中许多小到无法追踪，以每小时三万

cues.en: kilometers per hour.
cues.zh: 公里的速度移动。

cues.en: It would effectively create a deadly barrier around Earth, possibly too dangerous to cross.
cues.zh: 它实际上会在环绕地球的轨道上形成一道致命的屏障，可能危险到无法穿越。

cues.en: Dreams of moon bases, Mars colonies, or space travel at all may be set back centuries.
cues.zh: 月球基地、火星殖民地或任何太空旅行的梦想可能会倒退几个世纪。

cues.en: And the loss of our space infrastructure
cues.zh: 而我们太空基础设施的丧失

cues.en: would send some of the technology we rely on daily back to the nineteen seventies.
cues.zh: 会使我们日常依赖的一些技术倒退回二十世纪七十年代。

cues.en: But it might not be too late to clean up our mess. While the space industry has become better at avoiding space junk, it's still growing fast and occasional weapon tests don't help. So there have been of wild, but also serious suggestions about how to quickly remove as much deadly space junk as possible without creating more in the process.
cues.zh: 但清理我们的烂摊子可能还不算太晚。虽然航天工业在避免太空垃圾方面已经做得更好，但它仍在快速增长，偶尔的武器试验更是雪上加霜。因此，出现了各种大胆但也有严肃的提议，关于如何快速清除尽可能多的致命太空垃圾，同时又不在此过程中制造更多垃圾。

cues.en: Lots of ideas are being thrown around, and some of the most seriously considered involve capture and return missions, which are being tested now.
cues.zh: 人们提出了很多想法，其中一些被最认真考虑的方案涉及捕获和返回任务，目前正在测试中。

cues.en: One method involves meeting a piece of junk in orbit with a small satellite loaded with a net. Once caught, a small rocket could be used to bring it down towards Earth.
cues.zh: 一种方法是让一颗携带网的小卫星在轨道上与一块垃圾相遇。一旦捕获，就可以用小型火箭将其拖向地球。

cues.en: Targets too large for a net might be instead caught with a harpoon on a tether.
cues.zh: 对于太大而无法用网捕获的目标，可以改用系缆鱼叉捕获。

cues.en: Instead of firing a rocket, the cleaner would deploy a large sail to produce atmospheric
cues.zh: 清理器不会发射火箭，而是展开一面巨大的帆，以产生大气阻力

cues.en: drag and accelerate orbital decay.
cues.zh: 并加速轨道衰减。

cues.en: And there are lots of other wild sci fi sounding proposals too.
cues.zh: 还有很多听起来同样疯狂的科幻方案。

cues.en: Some might use giant electromagnets.
cues.zh: 有些方案可能会使用巨型电磁铁。

cues.en: These magnetic
cues.zh: 这些磁力

cues.en: tugs work by pushing on the magnetic components inside satellites that they use to stabilize and orientate themselves in Earth's magnetic field.
cues.zh: 拖船通过推动卫星内部的磁性组件来工作，而卫星正是利用这些组件在地球磁场中稳定自身并调整方向。

cues.en: These may be safer and more reliable than nets and harpoons because they never have to make contact with the junk they're handling, so there's no risk of accidentally breaking up their target into more junk. As
cues.zh: 这些方案可能比网和鱼叉更安全、更可靠，因为它们完全不需要接触所处理的碎片，因此不会有意外把目标打碎成更多碎片的风险。

cues.en: for the tiniest bits of junk, lasers might be the key to vaporizing them entirely.
cues.zh: 至于最微小的碎片，激光或许是将它们彻底汽化的关键。

cues.en: Satellites with lasers wouldn't need to visit their targets. They can shoot them from far away.
cues.zh: 搭载激光的卫星不需要前往目标位置，它们可以从远处射击。

cues.en: Large objects can't exactly be shot down, but lasers can be used to ablate them or burn tiny amounts of material off the side to push the junk to a safer orbit.
cues.zh: 大型物体当然无法直接被击落，但可以用激光烧蚀它们，从侧面烧掉少量材料，将碎片推入更安全的轨道。

cues.en: Whatever technology we use in the end, we better start doing something soon
cues.zh: 无论最终采用什么技术，我们最好尽快采取行动
否则一亿颗

cues.en: bullets become a trillion and the trap is set. If we don't act, our adventure in space might end before it's even begun.
cues.zh: 子弹会变成一万亿颗，陷阱也就形成了。如果我们不采取行动，人类的太空冒险可能还没开始就已经结束。
